tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Ashgrove Retail Group** operates an e-commerce platform and 60 physical stores. Online traffic is highly seasonal — flash sales and the holiday season can multiply load tenfold within an hour.

**Current Environment:**
- Production subscription with a web tier on **Virtual Machine Scale Sets** (uniform orchestration)
- Back-office batch processing packaged as **Linux containers**
- All infrastructure is deployed through a CI/CD pipeline
- The platform team is migrating its infrastructure-as-code from ARM JSON templates to **Bicep**

**Business Goals:**
- Absorb sales-event traffic spikes automatically without manual intervention
- Keep infrastructure definitions readable and maintainable for a growing platform team
- Minimize cost for workloads that only run occasionally

tabs.title: Technical Environment
tabs.content:
**Web Tier (VM Scale Set `vmss-web`):**
- Instance limits: minimum **2**, default **2**, maximum **10**
- Scale out: add **2** instances when average CPU > **70%** for 10 minutes
- Scale in: remove **1** instance when average CPU < **25%** for 15 minutes

**Infrastructure as Code:**
- Dozens of ARM JSON templates exported from existing deployments over the years
- New standard: all templates must be authored in Bicep
- Pipeline runs `az deployment group create` against the production resource group

**Container Workloads:**
- `inv-recon`: a nightly inventory reconciliation job in a single container; runs for roughly 30 minutes, then exits
- The operations team wants the simplest possible hosting option for `inv-recon` — no cluster, no environment resource, and per-second billing only while it runs
- Images are stored in an Azure Container Registry
